providers.description: AMMP (AMMP OS) is a distributed energy monitoring and operations platform for operators of commercial and industrial (C&I) solar and battery-storage portfolios. It unifies visibility across multi-vendor fleets, pulling data directly from more than 30 manufacturer cloud platforms and its own AMMP Edge data logger, and layers on monitoring, alerting, stakeholder reporting, commercial (SLA/cost) tracking, and customizable dashboards. AMMP OS monitors over 10,000 sites across 35+ countries and emphasizes vendor independence and ISO/IEC 27001:2022 certified security. Surfaced as a portfolio company of point-nine and enriched by the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Arrived
providers.description: Arrived is a real estate investment platform that lets individuals buy, own, and sell fractional shares of income-producing residential properties without the work of being a landlord. Investors browse curated single-family rentals, vacation rentals, funds, and real-estate debt offerings, invest in minutes, and receive passive rental income through dividend distributions plus potential appreciation while Arrived handles acquisition and property management. The company reports roughly 981K registered investors, $445M invested, and $95M distributed. Arrived is a consumer-facing investing product with a web and mobile app; it does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal, so this profile captures its public identity and domain-security posture.

providers.name: Probe Information
providers.description: Probe Information Services (Probe42) is an Indian company-intelligence and business-data platform that collects, cleans, and curates information on roughly one million Indian companies from 743 public-domain sources through a five-step verification process. Its products — Probe42 Business, Probe42 Banking, and the Probe42 API — deliver company profiles, financials, director and charge data, and risk signals used by banks, NBFCs, fintechs, and sales teams for onboarding, KYC/due-diligence, credit assessment, and lead intelligence. The Probe42 API lets developers embed this company data directly inside their own applications. Surfaced as an Accel portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment; the public API surface is gated behind developer-portal authentication.

providers.name: Zidisha
providers.description: Zidisha is a nonprofit direct person-to-person microlending and crowdfunding platform that connects funders in wealthier countries directly with low-income entrepreneurs in developing countries, with no local intermediary taking a cut. Founded in 2009 and backed by Y Combinator, Zidisha lets entrepreneurs apply for funding, communicate directly with their backers, post updates, and repay at zero interest so that funds recycle into new projects. The platform focuses on agriculture, retail, transportation, and small-business growth across regions including Kenya, Indonesia, Burkina Faso, and beyond. Zidisha operates as a consumer-facing web platform and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or integration surface; this profile tracks its public web presence in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Gilion (formerly ArK)
providers.description: Gilion (formerly ArK) is an AI-powered financial platform, headquartered in Stockholm, that sits between founders and investors to streamline how growth capital is allocated. For companies it offers non-dilutive growth funding for SaaS and technology businesses, including a Growth Loan and Seasonal Credit, underwritten by AI models of a company's trajectory. For banks, funds, and investors it offers an agentic-AI investment platform covering sourcing, due diligence, monitoring, and portfolio reporting. Gilion was rebranded from ArK and is backed by Creandum. The company publishes a public Trust Center (SOC 2 Type 2, CSA STAR, GDPR/CCPA/CPRA) but does not currently expose a public developer API; this profile tracks its security, compliance, and web presence in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Askria
providers.description: Askria (askRIA) is an AI-powered due diligence and deal-management platform that provides decision infrastructure for private capital. It builds digital twins of investment funds and runs three AI agents: Discovery for thesis-matched company sourcing and outreach, Due Diligence for auto-scoring deals against custom frameworks while surfacing gaps and inconsistencies, and Portfolio for post-investment metric tracking and performance monitoring. The platform generates Investor Readiness Scores and streamlines the funding lifecycle for both investors and founders under a usage-based pricing model. Backed by 500 Global.

providers.name: Clerky
providers.description: Clerky is an online legal service that helps startup founders handle their legal paperwork safely and efficiently. Designed by startup attorneys formerly at a Silicon Valley law firm, Clerky provides software and guided workflows for Delaware incorporation and post-incorporation setup, fundraising (SAFEs, convertible notes, board consents), hiring (offer letters, consulting agreements, equity compensation), commercial documents (NDAs), and ongoing corporate maintenance. Clerky is a Y Combinator portfolio company. It is a legal document assistant rather than a law firm, and does not currently publish a public developer API, developer portal, or programmatic integrations.

providers.name: Forecastr
providers.description: Forecastr is a startup financial planning and forecasting platform, founded in 2018 in Louisville, Kentucky, that helps founders and finance teams build investor-ready financial models, track cash flow and runway, plan headcount, budget expenses, and run what-if scenario analysis. It pairs cloud-based forecasting software (a spreadsheet-style formula builder, pre-built templates, drag-and-drop dashboards, and shareable live models) with fractional CFO services, and keeps actuals current through accounting integrations with QuickBooks Online and Xero. Forecastr is an API consumer of those accounting platforms rather than a public API provider; it publishes no developer API, OpenAPI specification, or SDKs at this time.

providers.name: HandUp
providers.description: HandUp is a San Francisco-based public-benefit crowdfunding platform that makes giving to nonprofit organizations and the people they serve easy, secure, and transparent. Launched in 2013 and backed by 500 Global and Version One Ventures, HandUp partners with 501(c)(3) nonprofits whose mission is to serve people experiencing poverty and homelessness. Donors give directly to individual campaigns or to pooled funds such as the National Fund and the HandUp Fund; partner nonprofits then distribute the donations to cover basics like food, clothing, and housing, and report progress and metrics back to donors.

providers.name: Herbie, Herbie Plan
providers.description: Herbie is an AI-powered estate planning platform and law firm that lets individuals and partner organizations create wills, trusts, and related legal documents online. Its agentic engine encodes the principles, laws, and practice of estate planning into a system that drafts and assembles documents at scale, paired with an AI copilot for natural-language guidance and optional attorney review through Herbie Legal. Herbie is offered directly to consumers and as an embeddable "estate planning as a service" offering for wealth management firms, insurance companies, and employers. Herbie was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Moneybox
providers.description: Moneybox is a London-based digital wealth management company, operating as Digital Moneybox Limited, whose mobile app helps people in the United Kingdom save and invest — round-ups on everyday spending, Stocks & Shares ISAs, Cash ISAs, Lifetime ISAs, general investment accounts, savings accounts and personal pensions including pension consolidation. It is authorised and regulated by the Financial Conduct Authority and appears in the UK Open Banking app directory as an account aggregator, meaning it CONSUMES bank open banking APIs to read customer transactions rather than publishing an API of its own. As profiled on 2026-08-26, Moneybox runs no public developer program: no developer portal, API reference, machine-readable specification, SDK, sandbox or partner API surface exists on any Moneybox-controlled host. The one machine-readable artifact it publishes is an RFC 9116 security.txt served from every moneyboxapp.com host.

providers.name: Pilot
providers.description: Pilot provides bookkeeping, tax, and CFO services for startups and small businesses, pairing purpose-built financial software with a team of finance experts and former operators. Its offerings include monthly bookkeeping, corporate tax preparation and filing, R&D tax credit studies, fractional CFO and COO support, and stock administration. Pilot serves venture-backed startups and growing SMBs, integrating with accounting and payroll tools to deliver accurate books and financial reporting. Pilot is backed by CRV, Foundry Group, Index Ventures, SV Angel, Techstars, and Union Square Ventures. As of this profile Pilot does not publish a public developer API or developer portal; its product is delivered as a managed service through its web application.

providers.name: Royal LePage
providers.description: Royal LePage is Canada's largest residential real estate brokerage brand, founded in Toronto in 1913 as A.E. LePage and operated today under franchise and corporately-owned brokerages by Bridgemarq Real Estate Services (TSX: BRE), an affiliate of Brookfield. It spans roughly 20,000 licensed REALTORS across 600-plus offices nationwide, and sits in the value chain as a brokerage/franchisor rather than as a data platform. Its consumer search at royallepage.ca is a downstream CONSUMER of listing data, not a publisher of it - the site states its inventory is "226,755 active MLS listings via the CREA DDF network," meaning the machine-readable feed belongs to the Canadian Real Estate Association's Data Distribution Facility, not to Royal LePage. On API posture the honest finding is that there is none published for developers - no developer portal, no documented API, no OpenAPI or OData $metadata, no RESO Web API or Data Dictionary certification anywhere in evidence (RESO is a US NAR-adjacent regime and is simply absent from the Canadian brokerage layer), and no SDKs, webhooks, or Postman collections. Account registration on the site creates a Virtual Office Website (VOW) relationship with Royal LePage Real Estate Services, Brokerage that restricts data to personal, non-commercial use, and the legal notice expressly forbids "spiders, robots, crawlers, data mining tools, or the like." Any programmatic access to the underlying Canadian listing record runs through CREA membership and the DDF licence, not through Royal LePage.

providers.name: Stash
providers.description: Stash is an investing and banking app that enables fractional share investing, automated portfolio building, bank account management with a Stock-Back debit card, custodial accounts for minors, IRA retirement accounts, and financial education content. Stash serves over one million customers and has $4.3 billion under management, offering subscription-based access to a hybrid DIY and robo-advisor investing experience starting at $3 per month.

providers.name: The Vanguard Group
providers.description: The Vanguard Group is an American investor-owned asset manager headquartered in Malvern, Pennsylvania, and is "the largest provider of mutual funds in the world" and the second-largest exchange-traded fund (ETF) provider after BlackRock's iShares. Vanguard manages approximately $12 trillion in assets as of 2025 and employs roughly 20,000 people (the "crew") as of December 31, 2024. The firm was founded on May 1, 1975 by John C. ("Jack") Bogle and is structured as a mutual: "Vanguard is owned by the funds managed by the company and is therefore owned by its customers." Salim Ramji was appointed Chief Executive Officer in July 2024. Vanguard's business spans index and active mutual funds, ETFs, personal advisor services, retirement plan recordkeeping (Vanguard Retirement Plan Services), institutional asset management, fixed income, and a financial-advisor channel served through Vanguard Financial Advisor Services. Vanguard operates across the Americas, Europe, and Asia Pacific. Despite that scale, Vanguard does not publish a public developer API program — there is no public OpenAPI specification, no SDKs, no CLI, no public webhooks, and no Vanguard-published public RSS feed. Investor, advisor, recordkeeping, and distribution-platform integrations are delivered through authentication-gated portals (investor.vanguard.com, advisors.vanguard.com, institutional.vanguard.com), PDF reporting, brokerage/custodian rails, fund-administrator data feeds, and industry recordkeeping interfaces.

providers.name: Empathy
providers.description: Empathy is a support platform that helps organizations guide people through loss, leave, and legacy moments, combining AI with human care to serve individuals navigating grief, estate planning, and major life transitions. Its products include LifeVault digital estate planning, Loss Support for beneficiaries handling claims and grief, Leave Support for employees during difficult life events, and Client Connect for advisors. Empathy sells to life insurance companies, banks and wealth managers, employers, health plans, and benefit consultants, covering 50M+ individuals. Backed by General Catalyst and Index Ventures. As of this profile Empathy publishes no public developer or API surface.

providers.name: RDP
providers.description: The Remote Desktop Protocol (RDP) is a proprietary network protocol developed by Microsoft that provides a graphical interface to connect to another computer over a network. RDP transmits keyboard, mouse, display, and audio data between client and host, enabling remote administration, virtual desktops, and remote work scenarios. The protocol typically operates on TCP and UDP port 3389 and is defined in the MS-RDPBCGR open specification. It is implemented by Microsoft's Remote Desktop Services as well as third-party clients across Windows, macOS, Linux, iOS, and Android. The RDP acronym is also shared with the Refinitiv Data Platform (LSEG), a cloud REST API platform for financial market data, historical pricing, ESG, and analytics.

providers.name: Rentals.ca
providers.description: Rentals.ca is a Toronto-headquartered residential rental marketplace and the flagship brand of the Rentals.ca Network, which also operates Rentfaster.ca, Louer.ca, Rentboard.ca, RentCanada.com and TorontoRentals.com across more than 100 Canadian cities. The network is owned and operated by Rentsync (formerly Landlord Web Solutions Inc.), which also acquired the research firm Urbanation in January 2026 and co-publishes the monthly Rentals.ca / Urbanation National Rent Report; Rentals.ca listing data also feeds a Statistics Canada rental housing index. In the Canadian real estate value chain it sits on the rentals side of the market, outside CREA's REALTOR.ca and Data Distribution Facility, which syndicate member boards' for-sale listings. Its API posture is honest but closed: rentals.ca itself publishes no developer portal, no OpenAPI, and no documented public endpoint, and the entire consumer site sits behind a Cloudflare managed challenge that returns HTTP 403 to anonymous clients. The real developer surface belongs to the parent, at the Rentsync Partners portal (partners.rentsync.ca, branded "LIFT System API"), which publicly names a REST API, an Ad Syndication API and a Search API but places all documentation behind an account whose registration form requires a written application explaining what you intend to build. There is no RESO Web API or Data Dictionary certification, no OData $metadata document, no Universal Property Identifier, and no open dataset published by the company.

providers.name: Dezerv
providers.description: Dezerv (Dezerv Investments Private Limited) is an Indian wealth-management platform building a house of investment solutions for affluent Indians. It offers discretionary Portfolio Management Services (PMS), curated mutual-fund portfolios, bonds, an Investment Portfolio Analyser (IPA), a Wealth Monitor for tracking held-away assets, and ESOP financing, alongside a research-led investment philosophy and a weekly money newsletter. Dezerv is a SEBI-registered Portfolio Manager (INP000007377) and Investment Manager to a Category-I AIF / Angel Fund; mutual-fund distribution is via its AMFI-registered subsidiary. The company is client-facing (client.dezerv.in portal) and does not publish a public developer API surface. This API Evangelist profile enriches the company identity, links, and security posture rather than an API.

providers.name: Hanover Park
providers.description: Hanover Park is an AI-native ERP and fund administration platform for private market investors, unifying fund accounting, portfolio intelligence, and the LP experience in a single system of record. It pairs a proprietary general ledger, waterfall engine, investor portal, and portfolio management layer with AI agents that read email, propose journal entries, and extract portfolio updates, all reviewed by expert fund accountants. The platform automates capital calls, cash reconciliation, general-ledger posting, KPI collection, and reporting for venture capital, private equity, and other private-market firms. Founded in 2024 and headquartered around a modern back-office thesis, Hanover Park raised a $27M Series A led by Emergence Capital (with Lux Capital and Susa Ventures) and has grown from $1B to $15B in assets under administration. The company is SOC 1 Type II and SOC 2 Type II certified with a zero-trust, client-isolated AI architecture. No public API or developer program is published at this time; the product is delivered as a login-gated SaaS application.

providers.name: Daffy
providers.description: Daffy (the Daffy Charitable Fund) is a modern donor-advised fund (DAF) platform that helps people be more generous, more often. Co-founded by Adam Nash, Daffy lets members set aside money for charity, invest it tax-free across ETFs, individual stocks, and 300+ crypto assets, and then recommend grants to any of 1.7M+ eligible US charities on their own timeline. It offers flat-rate membership pricing starting at $3/month, family funds for up to 24 members, advisor integration, and Daffy for Work employer giving. Daffy Charitable Fund is a tax-exempt public charity under IRC 501(c)(3). Backed by Ribbit Capital, it operates as a consumer fintech app with no public developer API surface as of this profile.

providers.name: Northwestern Mutual
providers.description: Northwestern Mutual is a Milwaukee-based Fortune 500 mutual insurance and financial services company founded in 1857, providing life insurance, disability income insurance, long-term care insurance, annuities, investment products, brokerage and wealth management services to individuals, families and businesses through a nationwide network of financial advisors. The company operates a large internal API estate — domain and experience APIs behind an API gateway, with GraphQL used to harmonize them — but publishes no public developer program, API documentation or machine-readable contract; its public engineering presence is an open source GitHub organization and a Bugcrowd-managed responsible disclosure program.

providers.name: PremiaLab
providers.description: PremiaLab is a portfolio performance and risk analytics platform for institutional investors — asset owners, asset managers, and consultants who collectively manage roughly $20 trillion in assets. Its platform provides a quantitative strategy database of more than 7,000 single- and multi-asset systematic (QIS) strategies from 18 leading investment banks, position-based risk analytics (stress tests, sensitivities and VaR across asset classes), the proprietary Premialab Pure Factors model for decomposing market risk premia, independent price verification with daily index-level reconciliation, and standardized QIS Index futures offered in partnership with Eurex. PremiaLab exposes a client-facing REST API at api.premialab.com that is protected by an OAuth2 / OpenID Connect authorization server; API access is provisioned for institutional clients rather than through self-service developer signup. This profile was surfaced as a Balderton Capital portfolio company and enriched from PremiaLab's public web and authentication surface.

providers.name: General Legal
providers.description: General Legal is an AI-native law firm for high-growth startups and SMBs, offering flat-fee commercial, corporate, and employment legal work delivered by U.S.-barred attorneys augmented with proprietary AI workflows. The firm focuses on contract review, redlining, negotiation, and drafting with transparent flat pricing (from $250) and fast turnaround (median under three hours), positioning itself as "outside counsel that scales like software." Practice areas include technology transactions, employment, data privacy, financial regulatory, blockchain/cryptocurrency, and emerging companies / VC. Founded in 2026 by Ryan Walker (ex-Casetext CTO), J.P. Mohler, and Javed Qadruddin, the company is a Y Combinator (W26) portfolio company that raised $11.5M across pre-seed and seed rounds. This profile was surfaced as a Y Combinator portfolio lead and enriched from public sources; General Legal is a legal-services company and does not currently publish a developer API.

providers.name: Liquidly
providers.description: Liquidly (Liquidly, Inc.) is a New York based financial technology company building infrastructure for illiquid assets — a permission-based secondary marketplace that lets holders of private fund interests transact without disrupting the fund. The platform serves three sides: fund managers, who get a streamlined and centrally supervised transfer process, market data, and the flexibility to structure longer lock-up vehicles; seller investors, who get a manager-approved selling process, access to a network of prospective buyers, and standardized commercial terms; and buyer investors, who get manager-granted asset permissions, standardized diligence materials, and technology-enabled execution. Liquidly targets the secondary market for the roughly $13.1 trillion invested in private funds across buyouts, venture capital, real estate, private debt, infrastructure, and growth. Broker-dealer services are offered through Liquidly IAS, LLC, registered with FINRA and a member of SIPC. Liquidly is backed by Anthemis, Portage Ventures, Village Global, and AmTrust Financial. As of this enrichment pass Liquidly publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or technical documentation; the product is reached through an authenticated web application.

providers.name: Prudential plc
providers.description: Prudential plc is a life and health insurance and asset management group incorporated in England and Wales and listed on the London, Hong Kong, Singapore and New York exchanges, with its principal operating office in Hong Kong and roots in London going back to 1848. Its home market for this profile is the United Kingdom, but its book is almost entirely Asian and African: life protection, health and medical, savings and retirement, takaful, pensions and Hong Kong Mandatory Provident Funds, plus asset management under the Eastspring brand, across Hong Kong, Singapore, Malaysia, Indonesia, the Philippines, Thailand, Vietnam, Taiwan, India, mainland China, Cambodia, Laos, Myanmar and a dozen African markets including Kenya, Uganda, Ghana, Nigeria and Zambia. It is no longer a UK retail insurer at all - the UK and Europe business was demerged as M&G plc in 2019 and the US business as Jackson Financial in 2021 - so the familiar UK "Pru" brands at pru.co.uk belong to M&G, not to this company. Its API posture is that there is no public API posture. Prudential plc publishes no developer portal, no API reference, no downloadable OpenAPI or Swagger document and no partner integration surface of any kind: developer, developers, docs, api, apis, partners, portal and sandbox subdomains of prudentialplc.com all fail to resolve, and /developers, /api, /developer, /partners and /integrations on the corporate site all return HTTP 404. The group's stated technology strategy is inward-facing - AI, automation, cloud and a global AI Lab running over a hundred internal use cases - and its distribution is built on tied agency forces and exclusive bancassurance partnerships with banks such as Standard Chartered, CIMB, MSB, SeABank, Bank Syariah Indonesia and UOB, which are commercial and contractual relationships rather than published API programmes. The Pulse by Prudential health and wealth app onboards health-tech and wealth-tech partners (Babylon, Tictrac, Halodoc, Smarter Health, Prive Technologies, OVO, Google Cloud) but every announcement describes the arrangement in commercial terms and none exposes a developer programme, SDK or public API. No ACORD, AL3, ACORD XML or NGDS reference was found anywhere in Prudential plc's public estate. Recorded honestly as a large carrier with a fully partner-gated, non-public integration surface. One genuine machine-readable surface does exist, and it is not an API: six of the group's market operating companies - Prudential Hong Kong, Prudential Singapore, Prudential Indonesia, Prudential Vietnam, Pru Life UK in the Philippines and Prudential BSN Takaful in Malaysia - publish real first-party llms.txt documents for grounding large language models, with Prudential Vietnam declaring a per-user-agent bot access policy for gptbot, claudebot, google-extended, perplexitybot and six other crawlers. The corporate domain publishes none. Underneath that, the group runs a visibly centralised security posture: TLS 1.3 and HSTS on every market host, and one shared PowerDMARC/PowerSPF tenant with a common aggregate-report mailbox across all seven domains, at p=reject on the corporate domain and p=quarantine in the markets, with no CAA record anywhere.

providers.name: Vennre
providers.description: Vennre is a Sharia-compliant private-market investing platform built for HENRYs (High Earners, Not Rich Yet). It curates and vets institutional-grade opportunities across real estate, private equity, venture capital and private credit from leading global managers, lowering entry thresholds so members can start building wealth from as little as $5,000. Delivered through a mobile app and web experience with a smart wallet, portfolio tracking and personalized wealth coaching, the platform is regulated in the UK as an appointed representative of Talbot Capital Ltd (FCA FRN 489839) and operates in Saudi Arabia under the Capital Market Authority (CMA License 19206-20). Vennre is a consumer wealthtech product; no public developer API or developer platform is published at this time.

providers.name: Crux
providers.description: Crux is a capital platform for the clean economy, connecting clean energy and manufacturing developers with buyers, lenders, and investors. Its marketplace facilitates the sale of transferable clean energy tax credits created under the Inflation Reduction Act, alongside debt capital markets, tax equity, and preferred equity solutions and advisory services. Crux pairs a transaction platform and secure data room with market intelligence drawn from tens of billions of dollars in deal data, serving project developers, manufacturers, tax credit buyers, banks, tax advisors, and legal teams. The company is backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) and was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead. Crux operates a customer application but does not publish a public developer API or OpenAPI at this time.

providers.name: PsyOptions
providers.description: PsyOptions is a decentralized options protocol built on Solana by Mithraic Labs, providing on-chain American-style options contracts originally designed for use with the Serum/OpenBook DEX. Rather than a hosted REST API, it exposes its functionality through open-source on-chain Anchor/BPF programs and first-party TypeScript client libraries (the @mithraic-labs npm scope: psy-american, psyoptions, market-meta, psy-token-registry, psy-metrics) plus a Rust crate. The project has since been sunset: its documentation and marketing sites are shut down, though the GitHub repositories and published packages remain available for reference. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Pantera Capital. Sector: crypto / DeFi.

providers.name: ServiceMax
providers.description: ServiceMax is asset-centric field service management (FSM) software that helps equipment manufacturers and service organizations maximize equipment uptime, optimize technician productivity, and streamline service delivery. Its cloud platform, built natively on the Salesforce platform (ServiceMax Core and Asset 360), spans work order and workflow management, scheduling and dispatch (Service Board), preventive and predictive maintenance, contract and entitlement management, parts and inventory, offline-capable mobile tools (ServiceMax Go), real-time technician collaboration (Zinc), and customer self-service (Engage). Founded in 2007 and acquired by PTC in 2023, ServiceMax integrates with PTC's IoT and PLM portfolio (ThingWorx, Windchill) and exposes its data and workflows through the underlying Salesforce API surface rather than a standalone public developer API.

providers.name: Structure
providers.description: Structure (Structure Financial Inc.) is a Web3 platform for designing, backtesting, and deploying fully automated, permissionless crypto trading strategies without writing code. Its visual strategy editor and AI-assisted code generation let users build algorithmic strategies that compile to Rust and deploy non-custodially to decentralized exchanges including Hyperliquid, Drift, and Jupiter; strategies receive trading-only permissions so funds never leave the user's vault. The company documents live, paper, and backtest execution paths and references MCP-agent and code-based access alongside its no-code visual interface. Founded by MIT and Jump Trading alumni and backed by the investors behind Coinbase and Solana.

providers.name: Bridgetown Research
providers.description: Bridgetown Research is an AI-powered research and analysis platform that helps organizations analyze businesses with speed and precision. Its AI agents conduct expert interviews, gather primary and secondary data at scale, and execute 300+ of the most common analyses to power autonomous market research and commercial due diligence. The platform serves private equity and venture capital firms, professional services firms, and corporate strategy and development teams, who access it either through a SOC 2-compliant SaaS platform with interactive generative-search reporting or via an email-driven workflow that returns PDF reports. Bridgetown Research also exposes a REST API (documented on Apidog at docs.bridgetownresearch.com) for creating research projects and managing experts, expert actions, and scheduled calls. It is backed by Accel and Lightspeed Venture Partners.

providers.name: Brookfield Asset Management
providers.description: Brookfield Asset Management (NYSE: BAM, TSX: BAM) is a leading global alternative asset manager with over $1 trillion in assets under management and approximately $614 billion in fee-bearing capital. BAM describes itself as "a pure-play, asset-light investment manager with earnings derived from stable, predictable fee-related revenue." The publicly listed manager was formed in December 2022 when it was spun out of Brookfield Corporation (NYSE: BN), which remains the majority shareholder. BAM operates across five investment verticals — Renewable Power & Transition, Infrastructure, Real Estate, Private Equity, and Credit — and adjacent Insurance Solutions capability is delivered through Brookfield Wealth Solutions, a sister business within the broader Brookfield ecosystem. BAM does not publish a public developer API program. Institutional Limited Partners, financial intermediaries, distribution platforms, and portfolio companies interact with the firm through private, authentication-gated investor portals, PDF reporting (10-K, supplemental, letters to shareholders), data feeds from fund administrators, and the investor-relations website at bam.brookfield.com.

providers.name: HELP
providers.description: This profile was surfaced as a portfolio-linked lead of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. The website pointer on this record resolves to Venturz (operated by GoVenturz, LLC), an all-in-one business operating system for founders that bundles 15+ tools — website builder, CRM, email marketing, payments, and analytics — behind a single dashboard alongside an "AI co-founder" assistant, a founder community, a startup academy, and Venturz Capital funding. As of this enrichment pass Venturz publishes no public API, developer portal, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI specification, SDKs, or /.well-known discovery surface, so no machine-readable API artifacts could be harvested. See x-identity-note regarding the stub name versus the linked brand.

providers.name: Tranched
providers.description: Tranched is a London-based fintech building an embedded, on-chain securitisation platform that connects fintech lenders and loan originators directly to professional investors. Its "Deep Tokenisation" approach represents loans as on-chain tokens governed by Smart Loan Agreements and automated waterfall contracts, letting originators structure and launch institutional-grade asset-based financing transactions up to 90% faster and at lower cost than traditional securitisation, with automated compliance, reporting, and monitoring. Tranched connects to a lender's loan management system via API integration to retrieve the data required for assigning and monitoring loans. Founded in 2023 by Clement Larrue and Michael Elalouf, the company raised a $3.4M pre-seed round led by Speedinvest in November 2024.

providers.name: The Block
providers.description: The Block is a New York-based digital-assets research, analysis, and news brand founded in 2018, covering cryptocurrency, blockchain, and Web3 markets. Its subscription platform, The Block Pro, packages breaking news, in-depth research, proprietary datasets, and venture-funding intelligence for professional investors, funds, and enterprises. The Block Pro also exposes a set of license-gated APIs - a real-time News API (REST, request-only, JSON), a Deals/Funding API, an Ecosystems/Data API, and a WebSocket news stream - available only to organizations holding a Block Pro subscription. The APIs have no public developer portal or OpenAPI definition; access and technical documentation are arranged through The Block's client-services team.

providers.name: Expansive
providers.description: Expansive is a Mexican real estate crowdfunding platform (crowdfunding inmobiliario) that lets individuals invest collectively in vetted real estate projects from as little as 1,000 MXN, earning returns backed by real guarantees. It operates as a regulated collective financing institution (IFC) under Mexico's Fintech Law and is supervised by the CNBV (Comisión Nacional Bancaria y de Valores). Expansive handles project vetting, funding, quarterly investor reporting, and payouts through its web platform and investor app (app.expansive.mx). The company is a portfolio company of 500 Global. It is a consumer-facing fintech investing product; it does not publish a public developer API, documentation, or SDK surface.

providers.name: GreenFi
providers.description: GreenFi is a climate-focused consumer financial technology company — the rebranded continuation of Aspiration's consumer banking arm. It offers a combined checking and savings account, high-yield savings with goal-based "Savings Pods", a debit card, a GreenFi Plus subscription tier, investing through its Redwood fund, and a cash-back Marketplace of sustainable brands, alongside impact programs such as Plant Your Change, tree planting and carbon offsetting. GreenFi is a financial technology company, not a bank; banking services and the debit card are provided by Coastal Community Bank, Member FDIC. Aspiration spun its consumer unit out in 2024 to Mission Financial Partners, LLC, which rebranded it GreenFi in April 2025; Coastal Financial Corporation acquired the GreenFi brand in January 2026. It is a separate company from Aspiration Partners, Inc., the enterprise carbon business that entered Chapter 11. GreenFi ships iOS, Android and web applications to end users and publishes no public developer program, API reference, or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: Percent
providers.description: Percent is a private credit platform that opens privately negotiated loans and debt financing from non-bank lenders to accredited and institutional investors, specialty-finance borrowers, and debt underwriters. The marketplace lets individual accredited investors access institutional-grade private credit deals (asset-backed securities and corporate loans) with entry points from $500 for direct deals, $5,000 for diversified Blended Notes, and $50,000 for Separately Managed Accounts, alongside a secondary market for eligible positions. Percent Securities, LLC is a U.S. registered broker-dealer and member of FINRA and SIPC; Percent Advisors LLC provides advisory services. Investor, borrower, and manager workflows run through authenticated portals; the public percent.com surface is marketing, education, performance, and regulatory disclosure. Percent has no public developer API — programmatic/deal-level access is not published.

providers.name: Scripbox
providers.description: Scripbox is an Indian direct-to-consumer wealth management and mutual fund investment platform operated by Scripbox Wealth Managers Private Limited. It helps families pursue financial freedom through personalized mutual fund recommendations shaped by expert advisors and data-backed algorithms, offering both regular (commission-based, zero monthly fee) and direct (advisory-fee) plans. The platform bundles portfolio construction and monitoring, financial planning, goal-based investing, tax-saving tools such as its Smart Withdraw algorithm, and multi-channel support. As of this enrichment pass, Scripbox operates purely as a consumer application and publishes no public developer API, developer portal, SDKs, or machine-readable API specifications.

providers.name: Black Unicorn Factory
providers.description: Black Unicorn Factory (BUF) is a Los Angeles based pre-IPO business accelerator that prepares companies led by founders from underrepresented communities for direct listings on national stock exchanges, positioning equity rather than debt as the route to capital. Its programs run a four-step readiness pathway — foundation and readiness assessment, compliance and corporate structure, SEC filing and disclosure, and market readiness — alongside the New Black Wall Street pre-IPO program and the Follow Me For Equity (FMFE) platform, an iOS and Android application through which individuals earn stock in participating pre-IPO companies by completing verified social engagement tasks instead of investing cash. Black Unicorn Factory is a private company whose shares appear on secondary marketplaces; it publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: Opto
providers.description: Opto (Opto Investments) is an end-to-end private markets investment platform built for wealth managers - RIAs, family offices, and private banks. The platform helps advisors build, fundraise for, and manage private investment programs across asset classes including infrastructure, private credit, private equity, real estate, and venture capital. Opto covers the full workflow: modeling allocations and automating operations to build a program, creating client materials and streamlining subscriptions to fundraise, and deploying capital with automated post-trade reporting to manage it. The company connects to existing custodians, investment-management tools, and reporting providers, and was surfaced as a portfolio company of 8vc. No public developer API or documentation is published at this time; access is through the advisor application and partner program.

providers.name: PartyDAO
providers.description: PartyDAO is the decentralized autonomous organization behind Party Protocol, an open, GPL-3.0 protocol for on-chain group coordination that aims to make Ethereum "multiplayer." Party Protocol lets groups form a Party (a shared Ethereum account with members, an inventory, and governance), collectively crowdfund to acquire assets, govern shared holdings, and distribute value to members — all through audited Solidity smart contracts rather than a hosted HTTP API. PartyDAO also ships Party (party.app), a consumer application built on the protocol. The developer surface is entirely on-chain: smart contracts, deployed contract addresses, and technical documentation for integrating via web3 libraries and direct contract calls. There is no REST/HTTP API, hosted SDK, or OAuth surface; integration happens by calling the deployed contracts.

providers.name: Step
providers.description: Step is an all-in-one mobile banking platform built for teens, young adults, and families. The Step Visa Card is a secured card that builds credit history reported to Experian, Equifax, and TransUnion, and teens can begin building credit before they turn 18 through parent-managed accounts. Step also offers savings rewards, cashback with partner brands, EarlyPay paycheck advances up to $250, commission-free stock investing powered by DriveWealth, early direct deposit, and the Money 101 financial education hub. Banking services are provided by partner Evolve Bank & Trust, Member FDIC. Founded in 2018 in Palo Alto by CJ MacDonald and Alexey Kalinichenko, backed by General Catalyst, and acquired by Beast Industries. Step publishes no public developer API; its programmatic surface is limited to a consumer service status page and a site llms.txt.

providers.name: Allocate
providers.description: Allocate is a technology platform positioned as an "operating system for private markets," enabling wealth advisory firms, family offices, and asset managers to source, transact, and manage private-market investments across venture capital, growth equity, buyouts, and private credit. The platform offers white-label fund creation for advisors, AI-powered portfolio management with document aggregation, curated manager access, and SPV infrastructure for aggregating smaller commitments. Allocate reports over $4.9B in assets on platform, 370+ wealth advisory firm clients, and 1,500+ manager relationships. It is a private company backed by investors including Anthemis, a16z, Portage, and M13. Allocate does not currently publish a public developer program or API; this API Evangelist profile captures its identity and public web properties.

providers.name: Launching Next
providers.description: Launching Next is a startup discovery and submission platform that publishes daily listings of new and trending tech startups and side projects worldwide. Founded as a long-running startup directory, the platform has featured over 45,000 startups and side projects, making it a go-to resource for founders, investors, and early adopters looking to discover what is being built next. Entrepreneurs can submit their startups for free, with an optional paid fast-track review.

providers.name: Nevis Wealth
providers.description: Nevis (Nevis Wealth) is an AI platform built for wealth management firms, giving financial advisors an AI assistant that automates administrative work — AI-generated meeting summaries, automatic task capture from client interactions, intelligent meeting-prep briefs, unified AI search across advisory systems, personalized client email drafting, and account-opening automation — so advisors spend more time with clients and less on paperwork. The company is used by advisory firms including United Capital, GC Wealth, Apollon Wealth, and Dodds Wealth, is SOC 2 Type I certified, and has raised $40M in venture funding. Nevis does not currently publish a public API, developer portal, SDKs, or developer documentation.

providers.name: PSD Citywide
providers.description: PSD Citywide is a SaaS provider of enterprise asset management (EAM) and public-sector software for North American municipalities and government organizations. Its integrated Citywide platform spans asset management, maintenance and work-order management, GIS integration (ESRI-powered mapping), permitting, planning and licensing with citizen portals, multi-year budgeting and forecasting, facility/space management (Spaces), and a field mobile app, alongside asset-management advisory and grant services. The homepage references a "robust API" for integration and customization, but no public developer portal, API reference, SDKs, or GitHub organization were found during enrichment; end-user product documentation is published in a HappyFox-powered help center. Added to the API Evangelist network via the norwest-venture-partners portfolio.

providers.name: Zarna
providers.description: Zarna builds autonomous AI associates for private capital firms — private equity, growth equity, private credit, family offices, and investment banks. The platform captures deal information from CIMs, emails, meetings, CRMs, and virtual data rooms into a structured institutional memory, then runs a swarm of specialized agents (Scribe for capture and logging, Memo for screening memos and briefs, Analyst for mandate-fit scoring, and Experts for warm-intro network mapping) that deliver finished work directly into Outlook, Teams, and Slack. Zarna integrates with 30+ deal tools including DealCloud, Affinity, Salesforce, and SharePoint, deploys into VPC or on-premises single-tenant infrastructure, and is SOC 2 Type II certified. A Y Combinator Fall 2025 company founded by an ex-AEA Investors team.

providers.name: Newfront
providers.description: Newfront is a modern business insurance brokerage and technology company headquartered in San Francisco. It combines a traditional insurance brokerage (commercial business insurance, employee benefits, retirement services, and risk management) with a software platform that gives clients transparent data and analytics to understand and lower their total cost of risk. Formed from the merger of Newfront and ABD Insurance, the company serves technology, venture-backed, and enterprise clients across property and casualty, health and benefits, and personal lines. Backed by Index Ventures, Susa Ventures, and SV Angel. As of this enrichment pass Newfront exposes a client-facing web application (app.newfront.com) but publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or machine-readable API specification.

providers.name: Every
providers.description: Every is an AI-native, all-in-one back-office and finance platform built for startups, unifying incorporation, business banking and cards, treasury and cash management, global payroll, HR and benefits, AI-assisted bookkeeping, and startup tax preparation (including R&D tax credits) into a single system. It offers free Delaware C-corp formation, business checking with cashback debit cards, treasury-bill and money-market investing, and bundled per-stage plans for new founders through established startups. Backed by Redpoint Ventures. Every does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or developer documentation; this profile captures its identity, commercial, and domain-security surface.

providers.name: Harness Wealth
providers.description: Harness — the company that launched as Harness Wealth, and today a wholly owned business of Multiplier, Inc. — is a New York City firm that runs an advisory platform for tax and wealth practices. It operates three connected surfaces: a marketplace that matches individuals with complex financial situations (equity compensation, liquidity events, business owners, real estate, high net worth) to vetted tax advisors; a client portal and workflow platform that tax firms run their engagements, documents, questionnaires and e-file on; and Harness Wealth Advisers, LLC, an SEC-registered investment adviser that recommends third-party advisers. Harness publishes no public developer program — there is no developer portal, API reference, OpenAPI/GraphQL/AsyncAPI specification, SDK, CLI or webhook documentation on any Harness host, and the product is delivered entirely as an end-user web application at app.harness.co.

providers.name: InvestaX
providers.description: InvestaX is a Singapore-based, MAS-licensed tokenization platform for real-world assets (RWAs), operated by IC SG Pte. Ltd. under a Capital Markets Services license (CMS100635) and a Recognised Market Operator license from the Monetary Authority of Singapore. The platform provides end-to-end infrastructure for the issuance, distribution, secondary trading, and custody of security tokens and tokenized securities, plus a Tokenization SaaS product for institutional issuers and RWA investment products such as tokenized money market funds and private credit. It supports multiple blockchain protocols including Ethereum, Polygon, BASE, Algorand, Tezos, and Hedera. Backed by 500 Global.

providers.name: Prescience Inc
providers.description: Prescience, Inc. is a Y Combinator (Summer 2026) health benefits platform for employers, building "healthcare for the age of abundant intelligence." It uses machine-learning underwriting to design custom, largely self-insured health plans that aim to cut employer healthcare spend 20-50% versus traditional PEO and insurer plans, pairing $0-deductible coverage, included GLP-1 medications, wearables, and a 24/7 AI Care Companion for members. The company sells to employers, private-equity portfolios, and providers, and publicly attests to SOC 2 and HIPAA compliance. As of this profile it exposes a marketing and member/employer web application only - no public API, developer portal, SDKs, MCP server, or machine-readable specification was found.

providers.name: Acretrader
providers.description: AcreTrader is a farmland investment platform headquartered in Fayetteville, Arkansas that lets accredited investors buy fractional, passive ownership stakes in individual US row-crop, permanent-crop and timberland farms. AcreTrader sources and vets each farm, then handles the legal entity, farm management and administration while investors earn returns from annual cash rent and long-term land appreciation. Securities are offered through North Capital Private Securities Corporation, a FINRA/SIPC member broker-dealer that is not an affiliate of the platform. Since 2018 AcreTrader has enabled investment in over 140 farmland properties spanning roughly 44,000 acres across 20 states, and its investment management arm, AcreTrader Management LLC, reports net IRR of 9.4% to 30.3% on realized deals. Proterra Investment Partners LP acquired AcreTrader in August 2025. AcreTrader publishes no public developer API, no developer portal and no machine-readable specification; contract discovery was run in full against acretrader.com and api.acretrader.com on 2026-08-10 and every discovery path returned 404.

providers.name: EquityZen
providers.description: EquityZen is a New York-based financial technology platform and marketplace for investing in shares of private, late-stage, venture-backed companies before they IPO. Founded in 2013, it connects accredited investors seeking access to pre-IPO equity with employees and early shareholders of private companies who are looking for liquidity, transacting through EquityZen-managed funds and secondary-market share sales. The platform handles the sourcing, legal, and administrative work of private-company share transfers. EquityZen publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documented API surface; this profile captures its company identity and domain-security posture for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Kita Bisa
providers.description: Kitabisa is Indonesia's largest donation-based crowdfunding and mutual-aid platform, founded in 2013 and headquartered in Jakarta. It lets individuals, nonprofits, and corporations raise and give funds transparently for medical causes, disaster relief, education, and community development, and operates a dedicated Islamic-philanthropy surface for zakat, wakaf, and qurban. The group has grown beyond crowdfunding into digital fundraising services for NGOs (ngo.kitabisa.com), a CSR and social-marketing practice for corporate partners (csr.kitabisa.com), a cooperative, and the SalingJaga mutual-protection and insurance product. Kitabisa publishes no public API or developer program — there is no developer portal, API reference, or OpenAPI definition on any Kitabisa surface, and partner integrations are arranged through business channels. It does run a substantial first-party open source estate of 75 public Go, TypeScript, and GitHub Actions repositories, plus a public responsible-disclosure program backed by an RFC 9116 security.txt.

providers.name: TIFIN
providers.description: TIFIN is a Boulder, Colorado based fintech company founded in 2018 by Dr. Vinay Nair that builds AI-driven wealth technology for financial advisors, RIAs, broker-dealers, asset managers and insurance firms. Its platforms span TIFIN.AI (an agentic operating system consolidating the group's AI businesses for wealth and asset management workflows), TIFIN Wealth (investment proposal, risk-capacity and client-personalization tooling that integrates with Fidelity, BNY Pershing, Black Diamond, Salesforce, Wealthbox, Redtail, Orion and iRebal), TIFIN AMP/AG for asset-manager distribution intelligence, TIFIN Give for charitable giving accounts, TIFIN @Work for workplace financial wellness, and Magnifi, an AI investing assistant. TIFIN incubated 55ip (sold to J.P. Morgan) and Paralel, and announced a joint venture, TIFIN.AI, with J.P. Morgan Asset Management. The company states its AI capabilities are available as APIs that plug into existing wealthtech stacks, but publishes no public developer portal, API reference, or machine-readable contract; access is gated behind a "Get access" request form.

providers.name: Vested
providers.description: Vested Finance is an investment platform that enables Indian residents to build globally diversified portfolios by investing in US markets. It provides access to 10,000+ US stocks and 2,000+ ETFs, professionally managed portfolios (Vests), global mutual funds spanning 50+ countries, and private-market opportunities, alongside INR-to-USD remittance handling and US tax-reporting tools for Indian investors. Vested also operates a login-gated Partner API developer portal at developer.vestedfinance.com that exposes its brokerage and investing capabilities to partners. The company was originally surfaced as a portfolio company of Techstars and is profiled in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Amperecloud
providers.description: Amperecloud (Amperecloud GmbH) is a German renewable-energy management software company whose cloud platform provides an operating system for monitoring, operating, and commercially managing solar, wind, and other renewable-energy assets at scale. The platform brings asset performance monitoring, maintenance and ticket management, commercial and technical asset management, and virtual power plant (VPP) capabilities into a single system, supported by migration, consulting, and custom-integration services. It is used by more than 300 customers worldwide managing over 8,000 installations and 10+ GWp of capacity. Added to the API Evangelist network as a point-nine portfolio company; no public developer API, OpenAPI, or developer portal is currently published, so this profile captures verified company identity and a domain-security probe pending any future public API surface.

providers.name: Corgi
providers.description: Corgi is an AI-native, full-stack business insurance platform for startups, offering modular coverage (Commercial General Liability, Directors & Officers, Tech Errors & Omissions, Cyber, EPLI, and fiduciary) quoted in minutes. Founded in 2024 and based in San Francisco, Corgi is a licensed insurance carrier rather than a broker, underwriting and issuing policies directly with pricing tailored to a startup's stage (pre-seed, Series A, growth). Backed by Kindred Ventures and TCV, the company was reported as an AI insurance unicorn in 2026. This API Evangelist profile was seeded from Kindred Ventures' portfolio; Corgi does not currently publish a public API or developer portal.

providers.name: Funding Societies
providers.description: Funding Societies (known as Modalku in Indonesia) is Southeast Asia's largest unified SME digital finance platform, founded in 2015 and operating across Singapore, Indonesia, Malaysia, Thailand and Vietnam. It provides small and medium-sized enterprises with business financing — term loans, micro loans, revolving credit lines, invoice and trade financing — and offers retail and institutional investors the ability to fund those loans for a return. The group is licensed and regulated in its markets and is backed by investors including SoftBank Vision Fund, Sequoia, and SoftBank Ventures Asia. Funding Societies does not currently publish a public developer API or SDK program; this API Evangelist profile captures the company's public web properties and security posture. It will be upgraded if and when a public API surface is published.

providers.name: HiJoJo Partners
providers.description: HiJoJo Partners Inc. (HiJoJo Partners株式会社) is a Tokyo-based independent asset management and fintech group, established in November 2017 and registered with the Director of the Kanto Local Finance Bureau (No. 3065) for Type II Financial Instruments Business, Investment Management Business, and Investment Advisory and Agency Business. The firm forms, sells and manages funds that give Japanese institutional and individual investors access to late-stage private and pre-IPO companies, and works to develop Japan's secondary market for unlisted shares. It operates three lines: HiJoJo Prime (in-person advisory for investors with 100M JPY or more in investable assets), HiJoJo.com (an online fund platform for individual investors with 30M JPY or more), and HiJoJo Private Market Solution for institutional investors and startups. HiJoJo joined the Nasdaq Private Market investor consortium in 2024 to expand secondary-market access in Japan. Its investor-facing platform is delivered as an authenticated member web application; the company publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK or machine-readable specification of any kind.

providers.name: Azura
providers.description: Azura is an onchain trading platform that lets users trade any onchain asset priced in USD without managing wallets, bridging assets, or paying gas fees. Under the tagline "If it's onchain, it's on Azura," the app offers cross-chain token swaps across multiple blockchains in a single transaction, spot trading with multiple order types, token discovery and analysis, portfolio and PnL tracking, a referral system, and an Azurite rewards program, all with zero platform trading fees. Smart-contract interactions are algorithmically security-audited. Azura is a consumer-facing DeFi product (web app at app.azura.xyz) backed by Initialized Capital; it publishes user documentation and a blog but does not currently expose a public developer API, SDK, or specification surface.

providers.name: BUX
providers.description: BUX is a European neobroker and mobile-first investing app operated by BUX B.V., a subsidiary of ABN AMRO. It lets retail investors across Europe buy and sell individual stocks and ETFs commission-free starting from as little as EUR 10, build automated BUX Investment Plans (thematic and expert-built portfolios), and earn interest on uninvested cash across BUX Basic, Plus, and Prime account tiers. BUX is authorised and regulated by the Dutch Authority for the Financial Markets (AFM), with client financial instruments and money held in segregated custody via ABN AMRO Clearing and deposits protected up to EUR 100,000 under the Dutch Deposit Guarantee Scheme. BUX does not publish a public developer API or SDKs; this profile captures the company's identity, legal, and security posture for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Abra
providers.description: Abra is a digital asset wealth and treasury management platform founded in 2014 that provides institutional-grade services for high-net-worth individuals, institutions, corporations, and family offices across all 50 US states. Its products include Vault (segregated-account custody built on Fireblocks MPC wallet technology), proprietary Yield strategies on BTC, ETH, SOL and stablecoins, crypto-backed loans up to 50% LTV, and institutional treasury management, OTC execution, staking, and advisory. The company reports $10B+ in transaction volume and $2.5B+ in loans processed, and is backed by Pantera Capital. Abra does not currently publish a public developer API, API documentation, or SDK surface; this profile captures its public identity and probed domain security.

providers.name: Arta
providers.description: Arta Finance (Arta Finance Wealth Management LLC) is a global digital wealth management platform that gives accredited investors and professionals from leading technology companies access to sophisticated investment strategies historically reserved for the ultra-wealthy and institutions. Its products include a High-Yield Cash Reserve (an automated U.S. Treasuries portfolio), curated private-market funds spanning private equity, private credit, real estate, venture capital and hedge funds, bespoke structured investments, private placement life insurance, and AI-assisted portfolio tools (AI for Wealth). Founded by former Google executives and backed by Ribbit Capital and other venture investors, Arta is an SEC-registered investment adviser (with a Singapore entity regulated by the Monetary Authority of Singapore), with clearing and custody provided by Pershing LLC. Arta operates as a consumer/member wealth application and does not publish a public developer API, SDKs, or MCP surface.

providers.name: Neara
providers.description: Neara is a physics-enabled digital twin platform for electric utilities and network operators. It builds a single, physics-accurate 3D model of a utility's entire network from LiDAR, GIS, and imagery, then runs engineering-grade simulations across vegetation management, wildfire and flood mitigation, severe-weather response, clearance and conductor-clash analysis, pole utilization and FEA, asset inspection and lifecycle management, and transmission and distribution network design. Utilities use Neara to plan, harden, and operate their grids at scale — forecasting and backcasting resilience, prioritizing risk, and optimizing capital spend across millions of assets. Founded in Australia, Neara operates regionally across ANZ, the USA, and Europe.

providers.name: Publishizer
providers.description: Publishizer is a book crowdfunding platform and literary agency that connects authors with readers and publishers. Authors create book proposals and run pre-order campaigns; readers pre-order copies to signal demand; and publishers use data such as pre-order volume and proposal quality to discover and acquire promising manuscripts. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes a consumer web platform and blog but no public developer API, documentation, or developer portal.

providers.name: Rheaply
providers.description: Rheaply is a circular-economy platform for enterprise asset lifecycle management. It gives organizations real-time inventory visibility, an internal reuse marketplace with approval workflows for reallocating surplus furniture, equipment, IT assets, and lab supplies, and sustainable disposition through a network of 3,400+ verified nonprofit and commercial partners. Rheaply helps companies, universities, and governments cut procurement costs, divert waste from landfill, track embodied-carbon savings, and run decommissioning and office move-outs. Backed by Techstars, the company operates a web application at app.rheaply.com. As of this enrichment pass Rheaply publishes no public developer/API program, SDKs, or OpenAPI surface.

providers.name: Safqah Holdings Limited
providers.description: Safqah Holdings Limited operates Safqah (Safqah Capital / Safqah Financial), a Saudi Arabian fintech platform headquartered in the Al-Malqa district of Riyadh and regulated by the Saudi Capital Market Authority (CMA). Safqah provides Sharia-compliant, debt-based real estate investment opportunities that let qualified individual and institutional investors fund real estate development deals starting from 1,000 SAR, alongside a financing arm that offers land acquisition, residential development, commercial development, raw land, and bridge financing to real estate developers. Investors track deal performance through periodic reporting and live project camera feeds. The platform is a consumer- and investor-facing web application with no publicly documented developer API, SDK, or integration surface at this time.

providers.name: Sidekick
providers.description: Sidekick is a UK-based online wealth management and investing platform that offers expert-led investments and savings products once reserved for the ultra-wealthy, delivered through a mobile app and web platform. Its product range spans managed investment portfolios, savings accounts, private equity access, and cryptocurrency exposure. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Seedcamp, Sidekick is a consumer (B2C) fintech and publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or API documentation as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: Titan
providers.description: Titan (Titan Global Capital Management USA LLC) is a New York City wealth-management firm founded in 2017 that offers app-based investing and advisory services to high-performing professionals and emerging high-net-worth individuals. Its product suite spans actively managed Flagship, Smart Treasury and Opportunities funds, direct indexing, automated stocks and bonds, venture-fund access, credit and real-estate strategies, crypto, and dedicated CFP-led wealth advisory, managing over $1.2 billion for 10,000+ clients. Titan is a consumer fintech application delivered via web and mobile apps; it does not publish a public developer API, developer portal, or API documentation. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of a16z, accel, and general-catalyst.

providers.name: caimitech
providers.description: caimitech.com is the domain of Wacai (挖财, Hangzhou Wacai Network Technology Co.), a Chinese personal-finance and wealth-management company founded in 2009 that offers accounting/bookkeeping apps, personal financial management (PFM) tools, wealth-management services, and credit solutions. Its developer surface is the Wacai Open Platform (挖财开放平台) — an HMAC-signed API gateway addressed by (api_name, api_version) pairs rather than REST paths, with first-party client SDKs in Java (published to Maven Central under com.wacai), Node.js, PHP, Go, and C#, plus a separate topic-based message gateway (pull/ack). Access uses an app_key/app_secret credential with MAC or RSA request signing and an optional token service. No OpenAPI document is published; this profile was enriched from the provider's public GitHub SDKs and package registries.

providers.name: City National Bank
providers.description: City National Bank is a national bank chartered in the United States and a wholly owned subsidiary of Royal Bank of Canada (RBC) since 2015, headquartered in Los Angeles, California and known historically as "the bank to the stars" for its deep roots in the entertainment industry. With roughly $98 billion in assets, it is an FDIC-insured, super-regional institution offering personal, business, and private banking, wealth management, treasury management, and capital markets services, with industry expertise across entertainment, healthcare, real estate, technology, and law. City National operates as CN Bank in Florida. It runs NO first-party public developer portal or documented public API: developer.cnb.com and developers.cnb.com do not resolve and api.cnb.com returns 404. Consistent with the voluntary, fragmented US open-finance model, consumer-permissioned account data is reached through third-party aggregators (Plaid, MX, Finicity, Akoya) rather than a direct City National API. As a covered depository institution it falls under the emerging CFPB Section 1033 Personal Financial Data Rights rule, but no City-National-specific 1033 or FDX participation posture is publicly documented. Its Canadian parent RBC runs a separate developer portal (developer.rbc.com) under a different charter that does not expose City National Bank APIs.

providers.name: Invesdor
providers.description: Invesdor is a pan-European crowdinvesting and digital investment platform that connects private and professional investors with companies raising capital through equity, subordinated loans, and bonds, with minimum tickets starting around EUR 250. Founded in Finland in 2012 and expanded through mergers with Finnest, Kapilendo, and Oneplanetcrowd, Invesdor now serves more than 180,000 investors across Europe and has channeled over EUR 600 million into more than 1,000 renewable-energy, scale-up, and SME financing rounds. It operates as a regulated investment firm under the EU Crowdfunding Service Provider (ECSP) regime. Invesdor does not currently publish a public developer API or developer portal; this profile tracks its public web, investor, and legal surface in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: CBRE Australia
providers.description: CBRE Australia is the Australian arm of CBRE Group, the global commercial real estate services and investment firm, trading locally as CBRE (Gwsla) Pty Ltd (AU09949) and operating across the Pacific from cbre.com.au. It sits on the advisory and management side of the Australian property value chain rather than the data-infrastructure side: capital markets and investment sales, leasing and occupier advisory, valuation and advisory services, property and asset management, and project and design-and-build delivery across office, retail, industrial and logistics, build-to-rent, and alternative asset classes. Its API posture is closed. As of 26 July 2026 no public developer portal, API documentation, machine-readable contract, or self-serve onboarding exists for CBRE Australia: developer.cbre.com.au, developers.cbre.com.au, api.cbre.com.au, and docs.cbre.com.au do not resolve, and the global developer.cbre.com host is NXDOMAIN as well. CBRE does run API infrastructure — api.cbre.com sits behind an Imperva WAF that returns 403 to every anonymous request, api-dev.cbre.com serves a default WSO2 API Manager landing page, and eipportal.cbre.com is a login-gated "Integration Platform" SPA — but none of it is published, catalogued, or reachable by an outside developer. Commercial listings are distributed through the cbre.com.au property search and Australia's portal duopoly, and CBRE's terms of use explicitly prohibit scraping property listings from the site. RESO is absent entirely, which is the honest answer for Australia: there is no MLS here, no RESO-certified Australian organization, and the country's mandated machine-readable property rail is PEXA's electronic conveyancing network, not a RESO Web API. Access to CBRE data in Australia is a client or partner relationship, not a developer signup.

providers.name: Rain Financial
providers.description: Rain is a Middle East and North Africa (MENA) cryptocurrency exchange and digital-asset platform, operated through Rain Financial Inc. and its Bahrain entity Rain Management W.L.L. Founded in 2017 by Abdullah Almoaiqel, AJ Nelson, Joseph Dallago, and Yehia Badawy, Rain became the first crypto-asset company accepted into the Central Bank of Bahrain (CBB) regulatory sandbox and, in 2019, the first CBB-licensed crypto-asset service provider in the region. Rain Trading Limited later received approval from Abu Dhabi Global Market's Financial Services Regulatory Authority (FSRA) to expand across the UAE. Rain lets retail and institutional customers buy, sell, store, and manage Bitcoin, Ethereum, and other cryptocurrencies against multiple fiat currencies, with a Rain Pro offering for advanced traders and the majority of customer assets held in multi-signature cold storage. The company raised seed, Series A, and a $110M Series B (Paradigm, Kleiner Perkins), and is a portfolio company of 500 Global.

providers.name: Savvy
providers.description: Savvy (Savvy Advisors, Inc.) is a technology-driven, SEC-registered investment advisory firm founded in 2021 and headquartered in New York, NY. It combines licensed fiduciary financial advisors with proprietary technology — including Savvy Intelligence, an AI workspace for advisors — to deliver personalized wealth management for high-net-worth individuals and independent financial advisors. Savvy manages $5B+ in assets across 100+ advisors in 30+ U.S. locations, custodying at Fidelity and Charles Schwab. The firm serves two audiences: clients seeking wealth management (financial planning, investment management, direct indexing, tax optimization, retirement, trust and estate planning) and advisors looking to join or build a practice on its platform. Savvy publishes no public developer API; this profile captures its identity, domain security posture, and the verbatim /llms.txt it exposes for agents.

providers.name: Slidebean
providers.description: Slidebean is a pitch deck and financial modeling platform for startup founders. It combines AI-powered presentation software that auto-designs investor-ready slides with professional pitch deck design services and financial modeling assistance for fundraising. Founders use Slidebean to build, refine, and share pitch decks, model their startup finances, and prepare for investor conversations. As of this enrichment pass Slidebean operates as a consumer/SMB SaaS product and does not publish a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or developer portal; its GitHub organization contains only forks and small internal JavaScript utilities.

providers.name: Cicada
providers.description: Cicada Securities, LLC is a financial technology company revolutionizing the bond markets in Emerging Markets. It operates an Alternative Trading System (ATS) focused on local-currency-denominated government bonds in Mexico (M Bonos, UDI Bonos, and Cetes), enhancing liquidity and facilitating all-to-all access in an anonymous trading environment through central limit orderbook and request-for-quote protocols. Cicada Securities, LLC is an SEC-registered broker-dealer and FINRA member, and Cicada SEF, LLC is an applicant for swap execution facility registration with the CFTC. The company offers a trading platform, live pricing data, and a programmatic API for direct access to LatAm local-currency rates market liquidity, backed by 500 Global.

providers.name: F.N.B. Corporation
providers.description: F.N.B. Corporation (NYSE: FNB) is a diversified financial services holding company headquartered in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, and the parent of First National Bank of Pennsylvania, an FDIC-insured, state-chartered commercial bank. With roughly $50 billion in total assets at year-end 2025, FNB is a regional super-community bank operating around 350 branches across seven states and Washington, D.C. (Pennsylvania, Ohio, Maryland, West Virginia, North Carolina, South Carolina and Virginia), offering commercial banking, consumer banking and wealth management through its eStore digital platform. On open finance, FNB exposes NO first-party public developer portal or documented API: the developer/api subdomains of fnb-online.com redirect to the marketing homepage and no developer documentation is published. Consumer-permissioned account and transaction data is reachable only through third-party aggregators (notably Plaid), not a first-party FNB API. No direct Financial Data Exchange (FDX) membership or public CFPB Section 1033 posture is documented by the institution as of this profile.

providers.name: iTrustCapital
providers.description: iTrustCapital (legal entity ITC2.0, Inc.) is a US fintech software platform for alternative assets, offering 24/7 self-directed access to dozens of cryptocurrencies and physical precious metals through three account types: tax-advantaged self-directed Crypto IRAs for retirement savings, Premium Custody Accounts (PCA) for everyday non-retirement investing, and Treasury Accounts for businesses, trusts, non-profits and other entities. The platform charges a 1% cryptocurrency transaction fee with no monthly, annual, startup, exit, storage or transfer fees, and runs a closed-loop system backed by third-party US banks, custodians (iTrust Custodial Services, Fortis Bank) and institutional storage providers. iTrustCapital is not an exchange, custodian, trust company, broker-dealer or investment adviser; all transactions on the platform are self-directed. As of this profiling pass the company publishes NO public developer API — its own help center states that it "does not offer any API integration to any third-party applications, including self-trading bots and coin trackers." Access is via the web app and the iOS/Android mobile apps only.

providers.name: LIQUiDITY Group
providers.description: LIQUiDITY Group (branded simply "Liquidity") is an AI-native private credit lender and alternative asset manager founded in 2018, headquartered in New York with offices in Tel Aviv, London, Singapore, Tokyo and Abu Dhabi. It underwrites and deploys non-dilutive debt and growth capital — typically $10M to $200M — to late-stage technology and mid-market companies across 35+ countries, using its proprietary DYNAMiCs decision-science platform to compress due diligence from months to days. The firm manages several billion dollars across multiple debt and equity funds, including Mars Growth Capital, a joint venture with MUFG Bank, and is backed by MUFG, Apollo Asset Management, Spark Capital and Meitav Dash. Liquidity is a lender that runs on software rather than a software vendor: its DYNAMiCs platform is operated for its own analysts, borrowers and fund investors at app.liquiditygroup.com and is not offered as a public developer product. No public developer portal, API reference, OpenAPI/GraphQL schema, SDK or machine-readable contract is published on any host the company controls.

providers.name: Tass Vision
providers.description: Tass Vision is a venture-backed technology startup that operates a product website at tassvision.ai. It markets two named products, SITRAC and VITRAC, each with its own product page and pricing page, alongside About, How It Works, Blog, Calendar, and Contact sections. The public site is a Vue single-page web application with Zendesk-based customer support. The company is backed by 500 Global and Big Sky Capital among a cluster of Central Asian venture funds and accelerators (IT Park Uzbekistan, Astana Hub, National UzVC, and others).
