Beyond capital the firm provides an immigration platform that handles founder visas at no cost, a mentorship network of founders and operators, and a fundraising engine for follow-on rounds. It was surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio entry of 500 Global; it is a venture firm and publishes no public API or developer program.

providers.name: 01 Exchange
providers.description: 01 Exchange (01.xyz) was a full-suite decentralized derivatives exchange on Solana, offering cross-margined and cross-collateralized Perpetual Futures and Power Perpetuals (SQUOL) built on a fully on-chain Serum limit orderbook, with support for up to 100 markets and 50 collateral tokens and up to 20x leverage. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of multicoin-capital and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. The people and product behind 01 are now part of N1 (app.n1.xyz), where trading, points, and rewards have migrated. This profile captures 01 Exchange's historical developer surface: the TypeScript, Python, and Rust SDKs and on-chain program interface published by the Zero One Global Foundation (github.com/01protocol).

providers.name: Alien Labs
providers.description: Alien Labs, Inc. was a San Francisco software startup founded by Cristian Strat, Mircea Pasoi and Liana Dumitru, and a seed-stage portfolio company of Bloomberg Beta. Under the Alien Labs banner the team shipped Summify, a social news digest acquired by Twitter in January 2012, and later Memo — "the wiki that's always up-to-date" — a Slack-native team knowledge base that let 8,000+ teams star a Slack message to save it as a searchable note, edit rich-text and code-block documents in context, and retrieve them with a /memo-find slash command. Memo stopped accepting new signups on January 16, 2018 and shut down on March 16, 2018; most of the engineering team joined Coinbase. The company operates no live developer portal, documentation, or public API today, and this profile is retained as a historical network record rather than an active API provider.

providers.name: Lettuce
providers.description: Lettuce (Lettuce Inc.) is a venture-backed startup headquartered in Venice, California, surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a 500 Global portfolio company. As of the July 2026 enrichment pass the company operates no live public surface: lettuceapps.com and every probed subdomain (www, api, docs, developer, app) return the same wildcard domain-parking page rather than first-party content, and no developer portal, documentation, API reference, OpenAPI or AsyncAPI specification, SDK, package-registry release, or .well-known discovery document could be located. The company's remaining public footprint is a GitHub account holding one internal Node.js proxy project and one empty repository. This profile therefore records verified identity and live probe results only; it is retained as a dormant portfolio lead rather than an active API provider, and carries no fabricated API artifacts.

providers.name: Mangata Finance
providers.description: Mangata Finance (Mangata X, since rebranded GASP) is a decentralized exchange built as a Substrate parachain in the Polkadot and Kusama ecosystem. It is designed for algorithmic traders and DeFi frontends, offering gas-free swaps, an omnichain ZK-rollup architecture, and a Proof-of-Liquidity consensus model where liquidity providers help secure the network. There is no REST or OpenAPI surface; developers integrate through a TypeScript SDK (@mangata-finance/sdk) that communicates with the Mangata Substrate node over Polkadot.js JSON-RPC/WebSocket, with published type-definition packages and open-source node, bridge, and dev-kit repositories under the gasp-xyz GitHub organization.

providers.name: Ulu Ventures
providers.description: Ulu Ventures is a seed-stage venture capital firm based in Palo Alto, California, founded by Miriam Rivera and Clint Korver. The firm applies decision analysis to venture investing and backs diverse founder teams, having funded 200+ companies producing 10 unicorns and 3 public companies over 14+ years, growing from $3.5M in initial capital to a $138M second institutional fund. Ulu Ventures publishes no public API surface; this profile captures the firm's identity, web properties, and probed security posture.

providers.name: VonBox
providers.description: VonBox operated as Vonjour (vonjour.com), a Santa Monica, CA cloud communications startup offering phone, text messaging, and contact center services for small businesses, backed by 500 Global (then 500 Startups) and Kima Ventures circa 2014-2015, including a Vonjour for 500 Startups perk program. The vonjour.com website is no longer live (DNS resolves but HTTP does not respond), and no public API, developer documentation, or client packages are published. The founding team (Daniel Tawfik, Aman Fahimullah) went on to build ZenPatient (zenpatient.com), a digital health platform, and the company GitHub organization github.com/Vonjour is now branded ZenPatient.

providers.name: Western & Southern Financial Group
providers.description: Western & Southern Financial Group is a Fortune 500 diversified family of financial services companies headquartered in Cincinnati, Ohio. Founded in 1888, the group offers life insurance, annuities, mutual funds, asset management, retirement planning, and investment management through a family of subsidiaries including Western & Southern Life, Columbus Life, Gerber Life, Integrity Life, Lafayette Life, Fort Washington Investment Advisors, Touchstone Investments, and W&S Financial Group Distributors, with over $112 billion in assets under management.

providers.name: Beacon (Software)
providers.description: Beacon Software is a permanent software holding company, founded in 2024 and led by CEO Nilam Ganenthiran, that acquires and operates essential vertical software businesses serving Main Street industries. Rather than flipping acquisitions, Beacon holds companies indefinitely, keeping each founder's team and brand intact while providing a centralized operating platform — engineering support, AI integration, sales, finance, and a network of portfolio operators — to help them better serve their customers. Backed by General Catalyst, Lightspeed Venture Partners, and D1 Capital. Beacon is an acquisition and operating company, not a developer-facing platform: it publishes no public API, SDKs, or developer portal.

providers.name: Broadvision
providers.description: BroadVision spans two chapters of Dr. Pehong Chen's technology work. BroadVision, Inc. (NASDAQ: BVSN), founded in 1993 and backed by Mayfield, was a pioneer of e-commerce and enterprise self-service portal software and later the Vmoso enterprise collaboration platform; the operating company was acquired by ESW Capital in 2020. The broadvision.com domain is now home to BroadVision Group (BVG), a US-based private asset management firm formed in 2006 that funds, incubates, and operates ventures across artificial intelligence, cleantech, fintech, healthtech, biotech, medtech, semiconductors, and cloud/big-data. The company does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Fnality International
providers.description: Fnality International is a London-headquartered financial market infrastructure company that builds and operates distributed-ledger wholesale payment systems settling in tokenised central bank money. Backed by a consortium of 24 global financial institutions — including Banco Santander, BNY, Barclays, BNP Paribas, Citi, Goldman Sachs, State Street and UBS — Fnality launched the Sterling Fnality Payment System (£FnPS) in 2024 as the first regulated DLT-based payment system supervised by the Bank of England, with US Dollar and Euro payment systems in development. The systems run on private Ethereum networks, giving participant banks 24/7 availability, real-time atomic and PvP settlement, programmable money and T+0 cross-border liquidity movement. Fnality Services is the operational and product-delivery arm that licenses software to participants and runs inter-system arrangements. Technical documentation for participants is hosted in a credential-gated Archbee space at docs.fnality.com; Fnality publishes no public developer portal, API reference or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: Jetapult
providers.description: Jetapult is a capital and support firm focused on scaling mobile game studios, combining operator-first funding with hands-on systems for monetization, user acquisition, market expansion, and operational efficiency. Its GamePac AI toolset helps indie studios create, grow, and monetize their games. Jetapult is backed by Accel and operates as a partner-and-capital platform for gaming studios such as Holy Cow Studio and UMX Studio. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network; Jetapult does not currently publish a public developer API, documentation, or SDKs.

providers.name: McGrath
providers.description: McGrath is one of Australia's largest residential real estate brokerage networks, founded in Sydney in 1988 by John McGrath and operating a mixed company-owned and franchise network of roughly 118 offices across New South Wales, Queensland, the ACT, Victoria and Tasmania. Its business lines span residential sales, property management and rentals, projects and new-development marketing, rural and livestock, an Asia Desk for offshore buyers, and mortgage broking through Oxygen Home Loans. Listed on the ASX in 2015 as McGrath Limited (ASX:MEA), it was acquired in June 2024 by a consortium of Knight Frank Australia and New Zealand's Bayleys for A$95.5m and delisted from the ASX on 28 June 2024. McGrath sits on the demand side of the Australian property value chain: it is a brokerage that publishes listings into the REA Group (realestate.com.au) and Domain portal duopoly, settles transactions over the PEXA electronic conveyancing network, and consumes valuation data from PropTrack and CoreLogic rather than producing any of those rails itself. Its API posture is honestly nil. No developer portal exists — developer., developers., api., docs., feeds., data. and portal. subdomains of mcgrath.com.au all fail to resolve (NXDOMAIN), and /developers, /api, /docs, /api-docs, /openapi.json, /swagger.json, /$metadata and /.well-known/openid-configuration all return HTTP 404. RESO — the only genuinely mandated machine-readable real estate contract anywhere in this study — is a North American standard driven by NAR and MLS membership; it has no Australian counterpart and McGrath has no RESO Web API or Data Dictionary certification, no OData surface, and no Universal Property Identifier usage. The only interoperability standards McGrath demonstrably implements are robots.txt and twelve XML sitemaps; every /.well-known/ document probed — security.txt, openid-configuration, oauth-authorization-server, api-catalog, ai-plugin.json — and /llms.txt return 404. Its robots.txt enumerates twenty crawler groups including GPTBot, ChatGPT-User, OAI-SearchBot, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot, Google-Extended, CCBot and Bytespider, but under RFC 9309 group-matching rules those named AI agents are disallowed only from Google Maps JS/RPC paths — the /properties/ and /search/ disallow lands solely on User-agent: *, so the listing corpus is nominally open to the named AI crawlers and closed to generic ones, while the properties-buy/sold/rent/leased sitemaps advertise those same URLs. Reachability is the harder gate: www.mcgrath.com.au sits behind a Vercel Security Checkpoint that answers scripted clients with HTTP 429 and a browser challenge on every path, so no unattended agent can read the site regardless of robots.txt. The listing inventory is a marketing asset routed to portals under commercial agreements, not a developer surface.

providers.name: Quantierra
providers.description: Quantierra (Quantierra Advisors LLC) is a quantitative real estate advisory firm that uses proprietary software to source, analyze, and execute real estate transactions on behalf of institutional investors, family offices, nonprofits, and everyone in between. The firm blends data-driven deal sourcing and quantitative underwriting with traditional brokerage and advisory services. Quantierra keeps a deliberately low public profile at the preference of its clients and does not publish a public developer program, API, or self-service platform; its technology is used internally to support client engagements rather than exposed as a product.

providers.name: Noetica
providers.description: Noetica AI is a New York-based legal and financial market-intelligence platform that uses natural language processing and a proprietary knowledge graph to extract, benchmark, and analyze deal terms from millions of public and private transactions. It serves transactional attorneys, capital-markets and M&A lawyers, credit and private-lending professionals, and legal-innovation teams at leading global law firms, delivering real-time quantitative and qualitative benchmarking across 60+ transaction types. Backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners and Thomson Reuters Ventures. As of this profiling Noetica exposes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, documentation, or /.well-known discovery surface; it operates as an enterprise B2B SaaS platform.

providers.name: Kinro
providers.description: Kinro is an AI-powered commercial insurance brokerage for small businesses, founded in the Y Combinator Spring 2026 batch and based in San Francisco. Its autonomous AI agents run the full broker workflow around the clock, from prospect identification and quote preparation through comparison, binding, and ongoing certificate and renewal servicing. Kinro targets the roughly 77% of the 36 million U.S. small businesses that are underinsured because traditional brokers cannot profitably serve low-premium accounts. It is licensed across 30 states, appointed by 15+ carriers with access to 50+ markets, and offers general liability, business owner's policies, workers' compensation, commercial auto and trucking, professional liability, cyber, and more. Kinro was surfaced as a Y Combinator portfolio company and enriched in the API Evangelist network; it currently publishes no public developer API surface.

providers.name: AMP Fund
providers.description: AMP (AMP PBC) is a public benefit corporation founded in 2025 by Anjney Midha, a former Andreessen Horowitz general partner, to build an independent "AI grid" — a pooled compute utility for frontier AI research teams. Rather than operating as a cloud provider or a conventional venture firm, AMP acts as an independent system operator: data center operators and labs contribute underutilized GPU capacity to a shared network, and member research teams draw base-load and burst compute from that pool at rates intended to sit below the volatile spot market. AMP pairs capital with compute, having raised roughly $1.3 billion for its first fund, and its PBC charter is structured so leadership can supply compute at cost without shareholder challenge. It has also committed a Public Wealth Fund of up to $500 million through 2030 toward education, workforce readiness, healthcare access, and economic resilience in communities affected by the AI transition. AMP publishes no public API, developer portal, or documentation surface as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: AssetWorks
providers.description: AssetWorks is an enterprise fleet and asset management software company with more than 40 years of history and over 1,000 customers across commercial and private fleets, government and public works, and higher education. Its products include FleetFocus fleet and enterprise asset management (EAM), Active Assets fixed-asset tracking, Recoup Ops surplus management, and Scan and Validate mobile inventory management. AssetWorks sells on-premise and hosted enterprise software to large fleet and facility operators; as of this profile it publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, or self-serve API program. This repo is a company profile in the API Evangelist network, backed by Battery Ventures.

providers.name: Kitchensurfing
providers.description: Kitchensurfing was a New York City marketplace that booked professional chefs to shop for, cook, and serve meals in customers' own kitchens, founded in 2012 and backed by roughly $20M from Union Square Ventures, Spark Capital, and Tiger Global. It began as an advance-booking platform for private dinner parties and pivoted in 2015 to a flat-rate on-demand model in which a chef arrived and cooked dinner within a fixed window. Neither model produced sustainable demand against better-capitalized meal-kit and delivery competitors, and the company discontinued service and shut down on April 15, 2016. It never published a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal. Its GitHub organization survives with eleven public repositories - open-source Ruby/Rails forks and internal hackathon projects, last active in 2016 - but contains no client library or API definition. The kitchensurfing.com domain was subsequently re-registered by an unrelated cooking-products affiliate publisher and no longer represents this company.

providers.name: Lemnos Labs
providers.description: Lemnos Labs, Inc. is an early-stage deeptech venture capital firm that invests at the earliest phases of hardware company formation, helping founders better understand their customer, anticipate problems, and leverage their assets. Lemnos contributes engineering, manufacturing, marketing, and financial capital alongside the check, and deliberately keeps a minimal public presence — its site is a single page that lists only the active portfolio. That portfolio spans robotics and autonomy (Built Robotics, Fort Robotics, Path Robotics, Scythe Robotics, Simbe Robotics, Petra), agricultural technology (FarmWise, Ceres Imaging), autonomous cargo aviation (Elroy Air), space data and precise positioning (Spire, Swift Navigation), simulation (Duality), video analytics (Lumeo), and physical security (Rhombus). Lemnos itself publishes no API, developer portal, SDK, or machine-readable specification; it is catalogued in the API Evangelist network as a venture-capital entity whose value to the network is its portfolio graph — several of its companies are meaningful API providers in their own right.

providers.name: liangyihui
providers.description: liangyihui is a company operating the web property at liangyihui.net, surfaced as a portfolio company of the venture firm Qiming and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public developer program: no developer portal, no API reference or documentation, no OpenAPI, AsyncAPI or GraphQL definition, no first-party SDK packages on any public registry, and no working /.well-known/ discovery surface. The public site is served from Chinese CDN infrastructure (Tengine / kunlunpi) behind a bot shield that answers every path with the same obfuscated JavaScript challenge, so the property soft-404s and cannot be crawled or inspected. A live API host does exist at api.liangyihui.net: it answers its root with a Tomcat-served "Welcome to LYH!" page and returns genuine HTTP 404s for probe paths, indicating a real but private first-party backend for the company's own clients rather than a documented public API. This profile records verified DNS, TLS and endpoint posture only; no API artifacts have been fabricated.

providers.name: New Residential Investment Corp (Rithm Capital)
providers.description: New Residential Investment Corp (NYSE: NRZ) was a mortgage real estate investment trust (REIT) that **rebranded as Rithm Capital Corp (NYSE: RITM) in August 2022** to reflect its evolution from a pure mortgage REIT into a diversified global asset manager focused on real estate, credit, and financial services. Rithm Capital is headquartered in New York City, led by Chairman & CEO Michael Nierenberg, and as of 2024 reported approximately $46 billion in assets under management, ~$5.2 billion in revenue, and ~6,045 employees across its operating businesses (Newrez mortgage origination/servicing, Genesis Capital business-purpose lending, Sculptor Capital Management alternatives platform, Rithm Property Trust REIT [formerly Great Ajax], Adoor single-family rental, Crestline credit, and Elecor Properties [formerly Paramount Group] office real estate). This profile carries forward the legacy `new-residential-investment` repo identity under the API Evangelist network. The active corporate identity, public filings, and investor communications are at rithmcap.com. Rithm Capital and its subsidiaries operate as financial-services businesses serving institutional investors, mortgage borrowers, and real-estate sponsors. None of the public-facing Rithm Capital, Newrez, Genesis Capital, Sculptor, Rithm Property Trust, Adoor, Crestline, or Elecor Properties websites expose a public developer portal, OpenAPI specification, REST/GraphQL API, SDK, CLI, webhook system, status page, or RSS feed. There are no public GitHub organizations of substance for any of the brand surfaces (the `newrez` GitHub org exists with zero public repositories; `rithmcap` does not exist). Integration with these businesses occurs through traditional B2B mortgage / capital-markets channels, not a public API surface.

providers.name: PKO Inc.
providers.description: PKO is a collective and investment group operating at the intersection of technology and entertainment. Describing itself as a community of founders, creators, execs, artists, angels and investors with more than 700 members, PKO runs online and offline networking events, mixers and collaborations, and invests in startups across metaverse, virtual worlds, VR/AR, web3 (crypto, NFTs, DAOs), the creator economy, gaming and esports, social media, platforms, marketplaces, communities, streaming video, and content and media. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network. PKO publishes no public API, SDK, or developer surface; founders submit pitches by email.

providers.name: SigFig
providers.description: SigFig is a San Francisco-based wealth management technology (fintech) company. It operates two lines: "Tandems," an enterprise platform that helps financial institutions deliver intelligent, personalized financial advice, and "SigFig Wealth Management," a consumer robo-advisory service that builds and manages tax-efficient, diversified investment portfolios tailored to each client's goals. SigFig is backed by Bain Capital Ventures, DCM Ventures, and Union Square Ventures. As of the 2026-07-21 enrichment pass, SigFig publishes no public developer API, SDK, MCP server, or developer portal; its site is served behind a WAF and the developer/docs/api subdomains do not resolve.

bands.blurb: Providers we have not scored yet — unknown, not zero.
